Recommend **publish-verified-testimony**.

The **monastery testimony is preserved**, while the **treaty protects the archive as the only evidentiary chain**. Authenticating and publishing the testimony brings lived memory back into public view without destroying the records needed to prove the **founding record was forged** and that **evidence identifies the falsifier**. This also answers the **council’s retracted admission** with evidence rather than making the testimony stand alone.

The principal tradeoff is delay. Verification postpones public release, giving the council’s retraction more time to shape public memory.

Reject **burn-archive** because it directly defeats the planning intent and destroys the only evidentiary chain. It would make the testimony unavoidable but harder to prove.

I deliberately excluded the **archive lantern’s repaired condition** because it does not affect testimony authentication, publication, or preservation of the archive. This recommendation creates no canon, Book Direction, or Canonical State.
